texto_para_tela: SINIXT · TRADITIONAL TERRITORY / “after her death in 1956, the government of Canada declared the Arrow Lakes Band extinct” / R. v. DESAUTEL · 2021 SCC 17 · APR. 23, 2021 / SUPREME COURT OF CANADA
credito_sugerido: Source: Supreme Court of Canada, R. v. Desautel, 2021 SCC 17, para. 6
nota: PENDENTE (Sala, item 7) → achado palavra por palavra, §6: 'Meanwhile, the population of Sinixt who had remained in Canada was small. By 1902, only 21 Sinixt still lived on their traditional territory in Canada, in the Arrow Lakes Band reserve. By 1930, only one person remained on the rolls of the Arrow Lakes Band, and after her death in 1956, the government of Canada declared the Arrow Lakes Band extinct, and the reserve lands reverted to the provincial Crown.' ([2021] 1 S.C.R., p. 549). Data do julgamento: '2021: April 23'. Quem libera é o verificador, com o redator.

Source: Supreme Court of Canada, R. v. Desautel, 2021 SCC 17, para. 6
texto_aprovado: The Arrow Lakes lie in the traditional territory of the Sinixt. In 1956, the government of Canada declared the Arrow Lakes Band extinct. Decades later, the Supreme Court of Canada recounted that history in a ruling. It found that a successor group of the Sinixt, based in Washington State, is an Aboriginal people of Canada.
